nodes.title: Part 1: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 1. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: What is LISP (Locator/ID Separation Protocol) and why is it used in SD-Access?
flashcards.back: In SD-Access, LISP provides the control plane. EIDs are IP/MAC addresses of endpoints; RLOCs are the tunnel endpoints (fabric edges). LISP Map-Server/Resolver manages the mapping database for endpoint mobility.

flashcards.front: What is VXLAN and what problem does it solve?
flashcards.back: VXLAN solves VLAN scalability in data centers and SD-Access. Each VNI (VXLAN Network Identifier) is equivalent to a VLAN but allows 16M overlays. VXLAN EVPN uses BGP for control plane.

flashcards.front: What is BGP Bestpath selection and what are the first three attributes checked?
flashcards.back: BGP bestpath mnemonic: 'We Love Oranges As Oranges Mean Pure Refreshment' (Weight, Local Pref, Locally originated, AS Path, Origin, MED, eBGP>iBGP, IGP metric, Router ID). Higher Weight/Local Pref preferred. highest wins) → Local Preference (highest wins) → Locally originated → AS Path length (shortest wins) → Origin → MED → eBGP > iBGP → IGP metric

flashcards.front: What is MPLS Traffic Engineering (TE) and what problem does it solve?
flashcards.back: MPLS-TE uses RSVP-TE to signal LSPs with bandwidth reservations. Allows routing around congested links even if IGP shortest path goes through them. Useful for WAN optimization and SLA guarantees.

nodes.title: Part 2: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 2. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: What is an OSPF virtual link?
flashcards.back: Virtual links are used when an area can't directly connect to Area 0 (temporary fix during network design). Transit area must not be stub. Configure on both ABRs: 'area X virtual-link [router-id-of-other-ABR]'.

flashcards.front: What is EIGRP Feasible Condition and Feasible Successor?
flashcards.back: Feasibility Condition: neighbor's AD < local FD. If met, that route is a Feasible Successor (FS). EIGRP instantly switches to FS on failure (active state avoided). Without FS, EIGRP queries neighbors (active state).

flashcards.front: What is Cisco ACI (Application Centric Infrastructure)?
flashcards.back: ACI: APIC controller + Nexus 9000 spine/leaf. Policy model: Tenant → Application Profile → EPG (Endpoint Group). Contracts define allowed communication between EPGs. Automates data center provisioning via REST API.
BFD sends hellos every 50-300ms (vs OSPF 10s default). Detects link failures in <1 second. Works with: OSPF, EIGRP, BGP, IS-IS, static routes. Must be enabled on both ends. Uses UDP port 3784/3785.

nodes.title: Part 3: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 3. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.back: NHRP is the 'phone book' for DMVPN. Hubs are NHS (Next Hop Servers); spokes register their IP. When spoke A needs to reach spoke B, it queries NHS, gets B's NBMA address, and builds a direct IPsec/GRE tunnel. allows spoke routers to dynamically discover the physical IP (NBMA address) of other spokes through the hub, enabling direct spoke-to-spoke tunnels in DMVPN Phase 2/3.

flashcards.front: What is Cisco IOS-XE vs IOS-XR vs NX-OS?
flashcards.back: IOS-XE: enterprise campus/WAN (ISR, ASR 1000, Catalyst). IOS-XR: service provider (ASR 9000, CRS, NCS) — microkernel, process isolation, ISSU. NX-OS: Nexus data center switches — Python API, vPC, FabricPath.

flashcards.front: What is LACP rate and what does 'fast' mode do?
flashcards.back: LACP timers: slow = 30s PDUs, timeout 90s. Fast = 1s PDUs, timeout 3s. Fast mode increases failover speed at the cost of slightly more control traffic. 'channel-group X mode active; lacp rate fast'.

flashcards.front: What is a BGP community and how is it used?
flashcards.back: Communities tag routes for policy. Example: ISP might accept 65000:100 to request lower local preference (deprioritize path). Well-known: NO_EXPORT (FFFF:FF01), NO_ADVERTISE (FFFF:FF02), INTERNET (0:0).

nodes.title: Part 4: Key Ideas
nodes.content: Quick primer on Part 4. Tap to flip cards covering the most-asked exam ideas in this domain.

flashcards.front: What is a BGP prefix list vs route map?
flashcards.back: Prefix lists are faster than ACLs for IP prefix matching. Route maps use match/set clauses for full policy control. Example: route map to set local preference for routes matching a specific prefix list. Applied to BGP neighbors.

flashcards.front: What is the purpose of OSPF Hello packets?
flashcards.back: OSPF Hellos are sent every 10s (broadcast/P2P) or 30s (NBMA) to 224.0.0.5. After Dead interval (4× Hello) without a Hello, the neighbor is declared down. Mismatch in Hello/Dead, area, stub flag, or auth = no adjacency.

flashcards.front: What is VRF (Virtual Routing and Forwarding)?
flashcards.back: VRFs partition the routing table: each VRF has its own RIB, FIB, and interfaces. Used in: MPLS L3 VPN (PE router has per-customer VRF), network device management (Mgmt VRF), overlapping address spaces.

Umbrella uses Cisco Talos intelligence to block malicious domains via DNS. All DNS queries routed through Umbrella resolvers. Provides: web filtering, malware blocking, DNS-layer security, and cloud-delivered CASB/SIG capabilities.
